info.title: Spacefast API
info.description:
API for sharing AI artifacts, managing spaces, claiming anonymous publishes, and operating versions.

The API is versioned in the URL path (`/v1`). Operations marked `deprecated` also send RFC 9745 `Deprecation` and RFC 8594 `Sunset` headers, plus a `Link` with `rel="deprecation"` pointing at the versioning and deprecation policy: https://spacefast.com/docs/api/versioning

oauth2.description: OAuth 2.0 with explicit Spacefast capability scopes. Use the authorization-code flow for people and client credentials for machines.

bearerAuth.description: Better Auth session, OAuth access token, OAuth client-credentials token, or sfm_ Space machine credential.

atomicApiKey.name: Auth
atomicApiKey.description: Spacefast API key in the wp.cloud `Auth` header. Accepted only by the wp.cloud-compatible `/v0/atomic-api` operations.

claimTokenAuth.description: Space key (sfc_…) for an unclaimed anonymous Space. Also the fragment of its claim URL and the token of its /__/<key> door. A publish without a credential returns it in `claim` with the claim link. With the key, `getSpace` extends the Space's expiry window, `getSpaceVersion` follows its publish, `createSpaceOpenLink` returns its reusable open link, and `restoreSpace` undoes a `deleteSpace` while the claim window remains open. The token of a push remote minted for an unclaimed Space (`sfp_…`, the password in its URL) is also accepted for API bearer authentication and keeps working after a claim that keeps agent access on. It cannot replace the Space key in the /__/<key> door.

sessionCookie.name: __Host-better-auth.session_token
sessionCookie.description: Signed-in browser session, set by the dashboard sign-in flow. An operation that declares only this one needs a person behind the request: an API key or machine credential is refused. The same session token is also accepted as `Authorization: Bearer`.

version.description: Must be the current platform policy version.

effect.description: Explicit deny always wins over allow.

items.description: Namespaced IAM-lite action (`noun:verb`), or `*` for all actions.

Resource URI from the resource union: stt://tenant/{t}, …/partner/{team}[/*], …/partner/{team}/principal/{id}[/*], …/principal/(team|external)/{id}[/*], …/site/{id}[/*], …/space/{id}[/*], …/site/{id}/space/{id}[/*], …/domain/{id}, or …/domain-group/{id}.

resources.description: Resource URIs this statement covers (wildcards cover subtrees).

conditions.description: AND condition attributes. Unresolvable attributes fail closed: no match for allow, and match for deny.

request.client.description: Restricts the statement to one resolved request client.

statements.description: Evaluation order: explicit deny wins, explicit allow permits, otherwise implicit deny.

metadata.description: Caller-supplied metadata.

secretPreview.description: Masked secret preview (prefix and last characters).

notBefore.description: Key is rejected before this instant.

expiresAt.description: Key is rejected from this instant.

ipAllowlist.description: CIDR/IP allowlist. Requests from other addresses are rejected.

createdAt.description: Creation instant.

updatedAt.description: Last update instant.

items.description: Connection id from `listConnections`.

stage.description: Current or most recently reported stage while work is pending.

capture.description: URL capture progress and advisory evidence; absent for other inputs.

id.description: Build id (`bld_`); opaque and never derived from a version id.

spaceId.description: Space (`spc_`) the build produces a version for.

status.description: Build lifecycle status.

kind.description: Build from an uploaded source archive.

ref.description: Branch, tag, or ref to build.

source.description: Publish provenance as declared at build start (client, git ref data, publish message). Present on failed and running builds too; the produced version's `source` is the authoritative copy once one exists. Null when nothing was declared.

retryOfBuildId.description: Original build retried by this build.

finishedAt.description: When the build reached a terminal state.

ruleName.description: The rule's name at the edge.

origin.description: Where the rule was declared: `file` in the space's own source, `config` in the live version's config, `overlay` in the space settings, `platform` by Spacefast.

reason.description: `fingerprint`: an earlier rule already does the same thing. `name`: an earlier rule already has this name.

CollapsedTrafficRule.description: A declared rule that an earlier rule already covers, so the edge never got it.

unread.description: Matching threads unread for you. Resolved threads are never unread.

author.description: Null for threads stored without an author: the `guest` filter value.

truncated.description: Whether a page, author or version list stopped early.

body.description: The reply's text. Null once it is deleted.

mentions.description: Spacefast user ids this thread or reply @mentions.

createdAt.description: When the reply was posted.

updatedAt.description: When the reply last changed.

deletedAt.description: When the reply was deleted, or null.

metadata.description: `edited_at` says when the author last changed the words. Any other key is deprecated.

edited_at.description: When the reply's author last changed its words. Absent if never.

status.description: `open`, or `archived` for a resolved thread.

editedAt.description: When the author last changed the thread's first comment, or null if never. Absent from an API older than editing.

name.description: Record name to create, relative to the zone.

value.description: Exact record value to set.

name.description: Canonical lowercase ASCII A-labels (IDNA2008/punycode), no trailing dot, no wildcard label.

unicodeName.description: Read-only U-label form, present only when it differs from `name`.

kind.description: Derived field, never create input: `apex` if and only if `name` equals `derivedGroup`.

wildcardEnabled.description: Whether wildcard hostnames can be derived from this record.

spaceId.description: Space this hostname selects (`spc_...`), or null when the record is inventory only. One Space per hostname; a Space may hold many domains.

primary.description: Whether this domain is its Space's primary hostname (feeds `liveUrl`).

redirect.description: Whole-host redirect target; present only on redirecting domains.

derivedGroup.description: PSL registrable domain of `name`; server-computed, never client-supplied.

registrar.description: Registration facet; present only on apex records.

dns.description: Authoritative DNS facet; present only on zone-cut-owning records.

hints.description: Projected domain hints derived from diagnostics, actions, observations, and operations.

createdAt.description: Instant when the record was created.

updatedAt.description: Instant when the record last changed.

deletedAt.description: Instant when you deleted the record. Present only on `deleted=true` lists.

managementKind.description: Derived DNS management state. This field is additive. `mode` remains the v1 compatibility field.

dnsMode.description: Hybrid DNS mode derived from `managementKind`: authoritative when Spacefast hosts the zone, or adapter when records are managed or observed on the user's existing host. This field is an additive read-model label.

provider.description: DNS provider key for a Spacefast-hosted zone, for example `spacefast` or `wpcom`.

assignedNameservers.description: Nameservers the registrar should use when Spacefast hosts the zone.

observedNameservers.description: Nameservers currently observed in public DNS; polled in both modes.

ownershipProof.description: The TXT record Spacefast DNS waits for before serving this zone. Add it at the DNS provider that answers for the domain now and keep the current nameservers until Spacefast sees it; Spacefast checks public DNS automatically. Present for Spacefast-hosted DNS; `null` when no proof is needed.

ownershipVerification.description: The ownership proof that Spacefast DNS waits for. Present for Spacefast-hosted DNS. `null` when no proof is necessary.

method.description: How the domain proves ownership. `nameservers`: set `assignedNameservers` at the registrar. The change is the proof, and Spacefast serves the zone during the wait. `txt`: add `ownershipProof` at the current DNS provider first, then change the nameservers.

reason.description: Why the method is `txt`. `conflict`: another person also claims this domain. `already_delegated`: the domain already uses Spacefast nameservers, so a change cannot prove ownership. Point it back at the previous DNS provider and add the TXT record there. `not_delegated`: the registry has no nameservers for the domain. `null` for `nameservers`.

expiresAt.description: When the claim expires. If Spacefast does not see the proof by then, Spacefast DNS stops answering for the zone and the records stay saved.

snapshot.description: Connected-provider record snapshot freshness for portfolio lists.

lastOperation.description: Latest DNS operation summary for portfolio and recovery surfaces.

url.description: Absolute URL to redirect to.

path.description: Path on the target space.

to.description: Redirect destination: an absolute URL, or a space (optionally with a path).

status.description: HTTP redirect status. Defaults to 308.

status.description: Registration lifecycle status; `expiring` is derived from the expiry date.

redemptionEndsAt.description: Instant when the provider grace or redemption window ends after expiry.

transferLock.description: Whether outbound transfers are locked at the registrar.

id.description: Registration or transfer record id; null when unregistered.

provider.description: Wrapped registrar bridge where the registration lives.

status.description: Registration lifecycle status. `pending_payment` means the purchase is not paid yet and nothing is registered.

expiresAt.description: Instant when the registration expires.

redemptionEndsAt.description: Instant when the redemption window ends after expiry.

autoRenew.description: Whether this registration renews on its own. On by default. Spacefast tells the team 60 days before expiry, then charges the paying team's saved payment method for one year starting at the current expiry. The first charge comes no sooner than 30 days before expiry and no sooner than a week after the team was told, so a name turned on, bought or transferred in later is told first and charged no sooner than a week after.

autoRenewChargesFrom.description: The earliest the next automatic charge can come, as of now. Null when auto-renew is off, the registration isn't active, the name expires too soon to renew on its own, or this term's renewal was refused by the registrar; renew it by hand then. It can only move earlier, once the team has been told.

failureReason.description: Provider failure detail when status is `failed`.

intentId.description: The purchase (`bpi_...`) this line belongs to. Read it with getTeamPurchase.

quotedFeeAmountCents.description: Registrar fee before tax, in cents.

paidAmountCents.description: What the customer paid for this line, tax included, in cents.

purchase.description: Money state of the current purchase, renewal, or inbound transfer line; null when none is in flight.

transfer.description: Transfer progress. Authorization codes are never returned.

authCodeDelivery.description: Authorization email request state. queued confirms provider queue acceptance, not inbox delivery.

offered.description: Whether a transfer can start now. The authorization code and the price are checked again when it does.

reason.description: Why not, when `offered` is false: `registration_active` (Spacefast already holds or is buying it), `domain_not_added` (a failed purchase released it), `transfers_unavailable` (not enabled for this team), `not_allowed` (this credential can't buy domains), `not_registrable` (not a registrable domain), `unsupported_tld` (an extension Spacefast doesn't register), `registrar_paused`, `no_price` (the registrar quotes no standard price for it), or `registrar_unavailable` (the offer could not be checked; try again).

DomainTransferInOffer.description: Whether Spacefast offers to move this domain's registration here. Connecting the domain works either way.

status.description: Current proof of DNS control. `failed` alone never tears down compiled serving state.

requiredRecords.description: DNS records the caller must create to prove control and route traffic.

lastCheckedAt.description: Instant when observed DNS was last polled.

lastVerifiedAt.description: Instant when this domain last proved DNS control.

diagnostics.description: Structured verification diagnostics with stable codes.

ipCidrs.description: IP address and CIDR Grants are unsupported because the serving runtime has no trusted visitor IP. Remove the IP constraint.

$schema.description: Canonical JSON Schema URL for this response body. The server also sends it in the `Link: rel="describedby"` response header.

type.description: Problem type URI resolving to the error docs page. The server derives it mechanically from `code` against the docs origin.

title.description: Short human-readable summary of the problem type. The server derives it mechanically from `code`.

status.description: HTTP status code of this response, repeated in the body.

detail.description: Human-readable failure explanation for this occurrence.

code.description: Stable snake_case error code naming the failed public contract.

pointer.description: RFC 6901 JSON Pointer into the failing request field, for example "/files/37/path", on validation failures.

details.description: Machine-readable context for the error code.

fix.description: One sentence on what to do about this error code, the same text as the `type` page. Read it before retrying.

suggestions.description: Actionable recovery steps safe to show in dashboards, SDKs, and CLI output.

next.description: Copy-pasteable commands or API requests an agent can run next.

requestId.description: The request id to quote when contacting support.

branch.description: Git branch the publish came from.

commit.description: Git commit SHA the publish came from.

message.description: Plain-language description of the publish (the version changelog entry, commit message, or release note). This is THE spelling for the publish description; the version files-diff API is the fallback when none is given.

dirty.description: Whether the working tree had uncommitted changes at publish time.

migration.description: Sent by earlier API versions only. Current servers omit it, and a Zero 0.8 app publishes as Zero 0.8.

remixedFromLegacy.description: Sent by earlier API versions only. Current servers omit it: any Space with no Zero yet may publish a Zero 0.8 app while Zero 0.8 publishing is on.

status.description: Operation-lifecycle status. Serving state is the separate `disabled` axis.

defaultHostname.description: Current Spacefast-owned managed hostname: under space.fast, or under view.fast for a space created before space.fast. Renaming the space changes the label and keeps the apex; previously managed hostnames temporarily redirect to the current one.

publicName.description: Public space label used in the managed hostname.

liveUrl.description: Live space URL: the primary bound domain when one exists, else the default hostname. Always present on non-deleted spaces.

sourceUrl.description: Deprecated alias of thumbnail.url. Send the same credential as for Space reads; this URL carries no access.

url.description: The Space's thumbnail endpoint on this API (`getSpaceThumbnail`). Send the same credential as for Space reads; the URL itself carries no access.

thumbnail.description: Server-selected dashboard thumbnail: a page screenshot, or a listing image, captured by Spacefast.

thumbnailUrls.description: The thumbnail in each frame a dashboard draws: `card` (802x552) and `hero` (a 2x capture), each for a light and a dark color scheme. Use a URL unchanged with the same credential as for Space reads; it carries no access. Null exactly when `thumbnail` is null; absent from an API older than this field.

dataLocation.description: Resolved data-location region, fixed when the space is created and immutable afterwards; "auto" only while no concrete region is known yet.

region.description: Deprecated alias of dataLocation. Current servers still send it for deployed dashboards; read dataLocation.

burstable.description: Whether this space's site can burst provider PHP workers.

archivedBytes.description: Bytes currently archived out of the hot runtime store.

hasRuntime.description: Whether this space's live version runs code and therefore has a Runtime surface. Feature eligibility alone does not make the surface visible.

channels.description: Channel pointers by name. "live" is present after a version is promoted.

config.description: Stored SpaceConfig overlay applied over the live version's sf.jsonc; null when nothing is overridden.

grandfatherBrandingRemoval.description: Whether this Space can keep removing the badge under a newer plan.

settingsDigest.description: CAS token for versioned settings writes (digest over title + config overlay). Send it back as baseSettingsDigest on PATCH to get compare-and-swap semantics.

noindex.description: When true, the live production hostnames serve platform noindex directives. True whenever the owning team hides its spaces from search engines (`teamAccessPolicy.noindex`), whatever this space's own setting. Immutable version and preview hostnames are always noindex regardless of this setting.

metadata.description: Your own labels on the Space. Absent from older readers.

teamAccessPolicy.description: The owning team's access rules that bind this space, or null when no team owns it. `privateSpacesOnly` means the space cannot be made public; `noindex` means it cannot be shown to search engines.

pinnedAt.description: Instant the space was pinned to the top of its team's space list, or null when it is not pinned. The pin is team-wide: everyone who can see the team sees it.

labelIds.description: Ids of the team labels on this space, ordered by label name. Empty when the space carries none. Manage them with PUT and DELETE /v1/spaces/{spaceId}/labels/{labelId}.

createdByUserId.description: User who created the space, or null when no account is recorded: unclaimed spaces, and spaces created before creators were recorded. Match it against the team's members to name them. Every caller who can read the space sees it, including the team's own dashboard. Treat an absent value like null.

viewerCanDelete.description: Whether the caller's account may delete this space. Team owners and admins can delete any space in the team; a member can delete the spaces they created. Absent on unclaimed spaces, which their space key governs, and when the request carries no account credential.

viewerCanTransfer.description: Whether the caller's account may transfer this space to another team. Team owners and admins can; a member who created the space can from the dashboard while nobody else has published to it and it has no custom domain, database, or paid resource. Present on single-space GET reads only; absent on lists, on write responses, on unclaimed spaces, and when the request carries no account credential.

audience.description: Who can open this Space right now. Spaces are private unless their Access settings say otherwise, so relay `audience.message` to the user whenever you share `liveUrl`. Present on single-space reads (getSpace, resolveSpace); absent on lists and write responses.

level.description: The access level as the dashboard's General access control names it: Private, Everyone in <parent team>, Public, Public with limits, Partly public, or Not verified. Absent from older servers.

message.description: Who can open this Space, as `Space access is: <level> - <who>`. Relay it unchanged to the user whenever you give them this Space's link, including after publishing.

parentTeamName.description: With `kind: parent_team`, the parent team whose members can also view the Space. Absent when its name could not be read.

viewerHasBar.description: Whether this Space shows the caller the Space bar, so a dashboard can offer to manage it on the Space itself. Decided server-side from the same rule the Space's runtime gets. Present on single-space GET reads for an account; absent elsewhere and from an API older than this field. Treat absent as false.

git.description: Git remote for this space, or null when it has no repository yet. Push to `remoteUrl` to publish.

visitedByHuman30d.description: Whether a person visited the Space in the last 30 UTC days: a successful request (status below 400) the host does not classify as a bot, platform requests left out. Null means unknown: the Space is not metered for that window. Display only; nothing is billed, limited, or disabled by it.

lastHumanVisitAt.description: End of the newest UTC day with a person's visit, so day resolution, within the last year. Null when unknown or none.

primaryContact.description: Who the team asks about this space. A label, not a permission: it grants nothing and the creator history stays separate. Null means the team admins, and every space on a plan other than Enterprise or Internal reads null; absent on unclaimed and host-managed spaces and for requests without an account credential. Change it with `primaryContactUserId` on PATCH /v1/spaces/{spaceId}; the accounts that may be named are `primaryContactCandidates` on GET /v1/spaces/{spaceId}/people.

SpaceBuildSettings.description: Repository build settings. Directory and command settings also apply to local builds.

services.description: Managed platform services (video, spam, uptime, search, backups, security).

index.description: Homepage file served at `/`; false serves no homepage. Folders always serve their own `index.html`.

fallback.description: Document served when no file matches. "/index.html" means SPA. Inferred for a single-page app build (200.html, _shell.html, or index.html beside a JS bundle with no root 404.html); false turns that off and serves the nearest 404.html.

path.description: Committed file served when no exact route matches.

status.description: Response status for the fallback.

cleanUrls.description: Serve flat `<name>.html` files at their extensionless URL (`/about` serves `about.html`). Defaults to on, so a committed page wins over the fallback; false hands extensionless URLs to the fallback.

meta.description: Listing, viewer, sharing, and browser icon metadata.

superpowers.description: Platform-managed built-ins and custom JavaScript snippets.

enabled.description: Enable customer-configured page enhancements.

disable_all_injection.description: When true, suppresses every platform-managed script/tag injection.

requireReview.description: When true, integration changes must go through review before release.

templates.description: Files that receive {{ vars.NAME }} substitution at finalize.

theme.description: Visual tokens for every Spacefast-authored page.

collab.description: Comments overlay delivery. `default` injects Spacefast's UI; `custom` injects only /__spacefast/collab.css for a self-built UI. Turning comments off lives in the Space's Comments settings, not here.

build.description: Default settings for remote repository builds.

edge.description: Run the redirects and headers the edge can answer at the edge, ahead of the space. Takes effect at the next publish. Off by default; the rules the edge cannot answer faithfully stay with the space either way.

markdownNegotiation.description: Accepted serving flag; runtime enforcement ships separately.

firewall.description: Requests to block or challenge before they reach the space.

name.description: Name for this rule: lowercase letters, digits, `-` and `_`, up to 61 characters. Names the rule in the CLI and the API.

action.description: `block` answers without reaching the space; `challenge` asks for proof of a human.

status.description: Status a blocked request gets. Defaults to 403. Blocks only.

any.description: Fire when any match field holds. Defaults to false: all of them have to.

items.description: Blocks or challenges requests before they reach the space. At most 47 authored comparisons; platform transport paths are exempt. An any rule uses one provider fence per comparison.

cache.description: Cache behavior, including which requests skip it.

bypass.description: Requests that skip the cache, in order. At most 50.

name.description: Name for this rule: lowercase letters, digits, `-` and `_`, up to 61 characters. Names the rule in the CLI and the API.

any.description: Fire when any match field holds. Defaults to false: all of them have to.

items.description: Serves matching requests fresh instead of from the cache.

source.description: Request path to match. * is a splat, :name captures a segment.

destination.description: Path or absolute URL. :splat and :name from the source are substituted.

status.description: Redirect status, 302 when omitted. To serve other content under this URL, use rewrites.

force.description: Answer even when the request path resolves to a committed file, the ! of a _redirects rule.

query.description: Query parameters the request must carry, as parameter name to capture name: { "id": "id" } is the name=:capture token id=:id.

redirects.description: Browser redirect rules. Same matcher grammar as _redirects, and _redirects rules match first.

source.description: Request path to match. * is a splat, :name captures a segment.

destination.description: Path to serve under this URL, or an absolute URL to proxy. :splat and :name from the source are substituted.

cache.description: Let shared caches store the proxy response. Absolute-URL destinations only.

force.description: Answer even when the request path resolves to a committed file, the ! of a _redirects rule.

query.description: Query parameters the request must carry, as parameter name to capture name: { "id": "id" } is the name=:capture token id=:id.

notFound.description: Serve the destination with status 404, the 404 of a _redirects rule. The destination must be a path.

rewrites.description: Rewrite and proxy rules: the URL stays, the content comes from the destination. _redirects rules match first, then redirects.

source.description: Request path to match.

remove.description: Remove this header instead of setting it, the !Name line of a _headers block.

headers.description: Response headers to set or remove on matching requests. A _headers rule wins on the same header name.

network.description: Enterprise network controls. Set this policy through the Space settings API.

allowedCidrs.description: IPv4 and IPv6 addresses or CIDR ranges that can reach visitor content.

ingress.description: Ingress policy that blocks visitor requests from all other source addresses.

dataSources.description: Deprecated (retired for new writes): named public WordPress sources exposed to repository builds; at most 32 entries. Set `WORDPRESS_URL` as a Space variable instead.

defaultDataSource.description: Deprecated (retired for new writes): name of the configured source exposed through `WORDPRESS_URL`. It must match a `dataSources` entry. When omitted, the first source in bytewise name order is used.

propertyNames.description: Stable source identifier: 1-128 letters, numbers, or underscores; starts with a letter or underscore; excludes __proto__, constructor, and prototype.

url.description: Canonical public WordPress URL: lowercase https:// scheme; IDNA-normalized DNS labels (1-63 characters each, 253 total, alphanumeric edges, alphanumeric or hyphen interior), canonical dotted-decimal IPv4, or bracketed hexadecimal IPv6; optional nonzero port and UTF-8 path. Percent escapes are validated and canonicalized; encoded percent signs, slashes, backslashes, controls, invalid UTF-8, whitespace other than encoded ASCII path spaces, credentials, queries, fragments, and trailing-dot hosts are rejected. Default port, host case, IDNs, dot segments, path encoding, and trailing path slashes are normalized before storage.

additionalProperties.description: A public WordPress site exposed to repository builds as a content source.

SpaceDataSources.description: Named public WordPress sources. Supports at most 32 entries.

wildcardEnabled.description: Whether wildcard hostnames can be derived from this record.

redirect.description: Whole-host redirect target; present only on redirecting domains.

registrar.description: Registration facet; present only on apex records.

dns.description: Authoritative DNS facet; present only on zone-cut-owning records.

hints.description: Projected domain hints derived from diagnostics, actions, observations, and operations.

name.description: Canonical lowercase ASCII hostname without a trailing dot.

unicodeName.description: Unicode hostname, when different from name.

primary.description: Whether this hostname is the Space's primary URL.

verification.description: Provider status and required DNS records.

servingRecords.description: Present when Spacefast DNS holds this domain's zone. Then `verification.requiredRecords` is empty, because the team adds no records by hand.

ownership.description: Present while this Space claims a hostname another Space holds. A claim reserves nothing and never expires.

status.description: `verification_required`: publish the TXT record in `verification.requiredRecords`, then verify. `moving`: the holder is letting go of the hostname.

source.description: Custom hostname attached to this Space.
Spacefast DNS holds this domain's zone.

hostname.description: Zone that holds this domain's records.

status.description: `served`: Spacefast DNS answers for the zone. `awaiting_proof`: Spacefast DNS answers after the team proves it controls the zone. `not_published`: Spacefast stores the zone's records but does not answer for the zone yet.

name.description: Hostname that this domain serves.

state.description: `served`: Spacefast's records answer at this name. `satisfied`: the team's own records already point at the Space. `blocked`: the team's records point somewhere else, so Spacefast writes nothing here. `pending`: the next domain check writes Spacefast's records here. `unknown`: Spacefast does not know the Space's addresses yet, so it changes nothing here.

records.description: Records that Spacefast keeps at this name. Empty while the name is blocked.

type.description: DNS record type.

name.description: Record name relative to the zone. "@" is the zone apex.

value.description: Record value.

blocking.description: The team's records that block this name. Replace deletes A, AAAA, CNAME and ALIAS records. It never deletes an NS delegation: the team removes that record itself.

names.description: One entry for each hostname that this domain serves.

SpaceDomainServingRecords.description: What Spacefast DNS serves at each hostname of this domain.

managedBy.description: Who owns the Git history. `spacefast`: push to publish. `github` or `connected`: deploys from an upstream repository; direct pushes are refused.

remoteUrl.description: Credential-free git remote to push to, or null for an upstream-managed repository. Authenticate as HTTP Basic user `t` with a space key or API key as the password.

repository.description: Name of the connected upstream repository this Space deploys from, else null.

defaultBranch.description: Branch that publishes to the live channel when pushed.

provisioned.description: Whether the repository behind this block exists yet. Always true for a GitHub binding; for a hosted remote, true once it was minted or first pushed to, and false while there is nothing to browse.

id.description: Stable managed row id derived from the default hostname row.

source.description: System-managed hostname row.

primary.description: Whether no custom primary domain overrides the managed URL.

name.description: Managed hostname.

publicName.description: Left-hand public project label for the managed hostname.

requiredRecords.description: DNS records the caller must create to prove control and route traffic.

lastCheckedAt.description: Instant when observed DNS was last polled.

lastVerifiedAt.description: Instant when this domain last proved DNS control.

diagnostics.description: Structured verification diagnostics with stable codes.

attachedAt.description: The first recorded time that Spacefast attached this managed hostname.

logo.description: Logo image (https URL or root-relative path) shown in the brand row.

name.description: Display name shown in the brand row of Pages defaults.

font.description: Font-family stack applied to Spacefast-authored pages.

hideSpacefastBranding.description: Remove the Spacefast badge from default pages when the plan permits it.

liveVersionId.description: Version that the live space URL now points to, if any.

pendingVersionId.description: Version that live traffic is trying to publish now, if any.

liveUrl.description: Live space URL. It moves to the latest version after a successful publish to `live`.

app.description: What the live version runs: its Zero app and its Functions worker, each null when the published tree carries none of that product (both null for a space without a runtime). The whole object is null for callers whose credential does not carry `versions:read`, because app details read version contents, not serving state.

pendingApp.description: What the pending version would run — the same projection as `app`, read from `pendingVersionId`'s version so a dashboard can show what an in-flight publish is about to serve. Null when no publish is in flight, and null for callers without `versions:read`, exactly like `app`.

principalType.description: Receiving principal kind: a first-party team or a host-managed external principal.

principalId.description: Tenant-local principal id: a team id or an integrator external customer id.

from.description: Current owner. Keeps full control, serving, and billing attribution until `completed`.

principalType.description: Receiving principal kind: a first-party team or a host-managed external principal.

principalId.description: Tenant-local principal id: a team id or an integrator external customer id.

to.description: Receiving principal. Accept is a to-side action.

status.description: Transfer state. Accepting moves ownership in one transaction, so a transfer is either still `pending_confirmation` or already terminal.

expiresAt.description: Instant when a pending transfer expires (default 7 days).

privateSpacesOnly.description: When true, no space in this team can be public: public Grants, public new-space defaults, and `access: public` on create or publish are refused with `team_private_spaces_only`, and public access declared in sf.jsonc is ignored. Turning it on revokes every public Grant on the team's spaces, turns `noindex` on, and blocks the team's share links (`blockShareLinks`), which on a parent team binds every subteam.

noindex.description: When true, every space in this team serves platform noindex directives on its live hostnames, whatever its own `noindex` says, and a space cannot turn it off. Always true while `privateSpacesOnly` is true.

shareLinksBlocked.description: When true, share links on this team's spaces open nothing and new ones are refused with `team_share_links_blocked`. Existing links are kept, not revoked: they work again once the block is off. A parent team's block binds every subteam.

parentTeam.description: The parent team whose members `parent_team` access lets view a space, or null when this team has no parent or its family is not on Enterprise or Internal. While null, `parent_team` is refused and stored parent-team access is inert: the space reads and serves as private, and creating, changing or revoking a public Grant meanwhile retires it.

id.description: The team id (the Better Auth team id in the main tenant).

name.description: The team display name.

slug.description: URL-safe team slug, unique per tenant.

role.description: Requesting member's role; member for non-session credentials.

roleVia.description: `direct` when the role was granted on this team; `parent` when it comes from being an owner or admin of the parent team.

slug.description: The parent team slug.

name.description: The parent team display name.

parent.description: The team this subteam belongs to, or null for a top-level team.

plan.description: Resolved plan code from the active subscription.

enabledAt.description: The instant this team became a partner.

partner.description: Partner access for this team, or null when the team is not a partner.

defaultDataLocation.description: Default placement region for new spaces; "auto" lets placement decide.

deletedAt.description: When you deleted this team. Present only in the `deleted=true` list.

metadata.description: Opaque team metadata stored by the client.

systemSpaceId.description: The space that supplies this team's page, theme, and presentation defaults.

key.description: The manifest key this item materializes.

state.description: Where the last reconcile landed this key.

placementReason.description: Why the rule runs at the space instead of the edge, or null for a rule that runs at the edge. `placement_off`: this space does not run its rules at the edge, so nothing about the rule was judged. Every other code is an `edge_ineligible_*` one, and says what about the rule the edge could not carry. `edge_ineligible_capture`: the rule captures part of the path, or its destination uses a capture. `edge_ineligible_condition`: it matches on a request fact the edge would read differently from the space, such as a country, a cookie, a query string, or the user agent. `edge_ineligible_destination`: it sends the visitor to another origin. `edge_ineligible_status`: its redirect status is not 301, 302, 307, or 308. `edge_ineligible_shadowed`: a published file already answers that path and the rule is not forced. `edge_ineligible_order`: an earlier rule that stayed at the space could answer the same request first. `edge_ineligible_reentry`: it is a rewrite, and the space has to match its own rules against the rewritten path. `edge_ineligible_proxy`: it proxies to another origin. `edge_ineligible_not_found`: it answers 404. `edge_ineligible_path_preservation`: it is a whole-host redirect, and the edge cannot carry the path across. `edge_ineligible_platform_header`: it sets or removes a header the platform owns. `edge_ineligible_header_folds`: more than one rule sets the same header, and the space folds them where the edge would replace. `edge_ineligible_quota`: the space has more placeable rules than the edge holds.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Required for the browser approval flow. Optional for a credential that has `tokens:create`. Use a client-generated key of at most 255 characters. The first request with a given key stores its outcome, scoped to your tenant, credential, and route. A retry with the same key and an identical body does not execute again: the server replays the stored response and marks it `Idempotency-Replayed: true`. A request that reuses a key with a different body fails with 409 `idempotency_key_reused`. A duplicate request that arrives while the first is still in flight fails with 409 `idempotency_conflict_in_progress`. The server keeps each key for 24 hours.

post.summary: Register, renew, or transfer a domain
post.description: `renew` and `purchase` (a one-name purchaseDomain) create a team purchase and return it in `data.purchase`, under the same rule as purchaseDomain: with purchasing power and `expectedTotalCents` the saved payment method is charged now, otherwise give the user `purchase.confirmUrl`. This also applies without X-Spacefast-Client. The registrar is asked only after payment; poll getDomainRegistration for the outcome. Released Spacefast CLIs before 0.9.0, identified by their capabilities header without X-Spacefast-Cli-Version, are never charged from expectedTotalCents: the purchase is held for a person, and the receipt adds the `checkout` pay link those CLIs read. Transfers require the `domains.transfers` feature. `transfer_in` checks the authorization code and registry locks, then creates a team purchase the same way, with the saved `contactId`; DNS stays unchanged. `transfer_out` queues unlocking and an authorization email to the registrant, then returns an operation. Only a current owner or admin of the domain's team transfers a domain out, acting as themselves; a team key is refused with `domain_transfer_forbidden`, and an agent grant asks its person first (`confirmation_required`). A domain registered, transferred in or moved to another registrant less than 60 days ago is refused with `domain_transfer_locked` and the lock's end in `details.lockedUntil`. Use the code at the gaining registrar. Email success means queued, not delivered; neither command acceptance nor unlocking proves completion. `resendAuthCode=true` explicitly requests another email after checking the inbox. Poll the registration transfer state for completion.

patch.description: Changes settings of a domain the team registered through Spacefast: `transferLock: true` (relocks at the registrar and remains available with transfers disabled; send it on its own, with no other setting; unlock with the `transfer_out` registration action), WHOIS `privacySetting`, the registrant (`contactId` of a saved contact), and the `autoRenew` preference. Privacy and registrant changes reach the registrar first and are saved only once it accepts: a refusal answers 409 (`domain_transfer_locked`, `domain_registrar_disputed` or `domain_registrar_inactive`) and changes nothing, and an unconfirmed write answers 503 `domain_registration_unconfirmed`; send the same change again. A new registrant starts the registry's 60-day transfer lock. Editing a saved contact updates every registration using it at the registrar. A domain belongs to the person whose contact it is registered to: only they move it to another contact, and only to one of their own. Unlocking transfers, turning off privacy, or changing the registrant affects who controls the domain and whose details are public, so make those changes only at the user's request. `autoRenew` is on for every registration unless its owner turns it off. While on, Spacefast notifies the team's owners and admins in the dashboard's Notifications 60 days before expiry (no email), then renews the domain for a year from its current expiry, charging the paying team's saved payment method from 30 days before it expires and retrying until it does; nothing is tried once it has expired. A name the team first hears about inside 37 days (turned on, bought or transferred in late) is charged no sooner than a week after that notice; `autoRenewChargesFrom` on the registration gives the earliest charge, or null when auto-renew can't renew this term. A term nobody was told about is never charged: a paying team with no owner or admin is not charged, and `autoRenewChargesFrom` is null until it has one, who is then told and charged no sooner than a week later. Turning it off releases any automatic renewal not yet charged. A missing payment method or a declined charge can still stop it. A person can still renew it early with the `renew` registration action.

post.summary: Publish files or capture a website and get a live URL
post.description: Publish files, a zip/tar archive, or a public HTTPS website and get a Spacefast URL. Pass sourceUrl to capture and publish a website; it is mutually exclusive with files, deletions, and archive uploads. Through an OAuth grant or the hosted MCP server, sourceUrl must be on a domain the team controls in Spacefast: registered through Spacefast, or with a proven Spacefast DNS zone. Other URLs fail with 403 source_url_domain_unverified. URL publishes and archives that need a build return a durable Build receipt with next.action=poll; follow links.status until publication completes. The Build's capture field reports URL capture progress and quality evidence; an unmeasured visual comparison is not a passing comparison. Use a stable Idempotency-Key when retrying the same request. Already-built files and static website archives publish directly and wait for finalization by default; pass async=1 to return an operation link to poll instead. For buildable source on a Spacefast-managed Space, the receipt's git block provides the repository remote and the Build's input.commit identifies the source commit; later git pushes continue that repository history. The Open link provides reusable access. A new team Space starts with the team's default access unless you pass access. Pass spaceId to update an existing Space; otherwise a new Space is created.

parameters.name: async
parameters.description: Controls the finalize transport. Omit the parameter, or pass `0` or `false`, to wait for the finalize and return the terminal receipt, degrading to a poll receipt only at the in-request ceiling. Pass `1` or `true` to return immediately with the operation to poll. Project archives always return a durable Build receipt and poll URL instead of holding the request open.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Optional client-generated key, at most 255 characters, that makes this write safe to retry. The first request with a given key stores its outcome, scoped to your tenant, credential, and route. A retry with the same key and an identical body does not execute again: the server replays the stored response and marks it `Idempotency-Replayed: true`. A credential-free publish request that sends this header must also send X-Spacefast-Idempotency-Principal. A request that reuses a key with a different body fails with 409 `idempotency_key_reused`. A duplicate request that arrives while the first is still in flight fails with 409 `idempotency_conflict_in_progress`. The server keeps each key for 24 hours.

parameters.name: X-Spacefast-Idempotency-Principal
parameters.description: Required with Idempotency-Key on a credential-free publish. Send a stable 64-character hexadecimal value that only the caller knows, and send it unchanged on every retry. It isolates the stored one-time claim and upload credentials from other anonymous callers. Never log or share this value.

post.summary: Mint a Git remote for a Space that does not exist yet
post.description: Returns a signed Git remote and the id of the Space it creates. The first `git push` to it creates that Space, in `teamId` when signed in or as an anonymous claimable Space when signed out, and starts its first build; until then nothing is created and `GET /v1/spaces/{spaceId}` returns 404. The last path segment of the push URL names the Space: replace it with a URL-encoded name before the first push, or keep it to get a generated name. An anonymous remote also returns the Space's key, which reads the Space once it exists. The remote's own token (the password in its URL) is accepted wherever that key is, and after a claim that keeps agent access on it acts as the Space's continuation API key.

level.description: The access level as the dashboard's General access control names it: Private, Everyone in <parent team>, Public, Public with limits, Partly public, or Not verified. Absent from older servers.

message.description: Who can open this Space, as `Space access is: <level> - <who>`. Relay it unchanged to the user whenever you give them this Space's link, including after publishing.

parentTeamName.description: With `kind: parent_team`, the parent team whose members can also view the Space. Absent when its name could not be read.

viewerHasBar.description: Whether this Space shows the caller the Space bar, so a dashboard can offer to manage it on the Space itself. Decided server-side from the same rule the Space's runtime gets. Present on single-space GET reads for an account; absent elsewhere and from an API older than this field. Treat absent as false.

git.description: Git remote for this space, or null when it has no repository yet. Push to `remoteUrl` to publish.

visitedByHuman30d.description: Whether a person visited the Space in the last 30 UTC days: a successful request (status below 400) the host does not classify as a bot, platform requests left out. Null means unknown: the Space is not metered for that window. Display only; nothing is billed, limited, or disabled by it.

lastHumanVisitAt.description: End of the newest UTC day with a person's visit, so day resolution, within the last year. Null when unknown or none.

primaryContact.description: Who the team asks about this space. A label, not a permission: it grants nothing and the creator history stays separate. Null means the team admins, and every space on a plan other than Enterprise or Internal reads null; absent on unclaimed and host-managed spaces and for requests without an account credential. invitation.description: For via=invite: pending until the person accepts it on the sign-in page.

openWithAccount.description: Open this URL through POST /v1/spaces/{id}/open using its hostname and pathname.

openUrl.description: Destination for a shared Space; use openSpace first when openWithAccount is true.

default.description: Problem details (RFC 9457). Any 4xx/5xx response is one `application/problem+json` document.

post.description: Creates a space under a team with a chosen or generated slug. Pass `source` to create it from a repository and start its first build; the receipt's `operation` tracks the copy. Use POST /v1/publish to create a space and publish content in one call.

post.description: Creates a build that produces a version on success through the normal publish path. Repository inputs use the saved connection; source archive inputs receive an upload instruction the new build owns.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Optional client-generated key, at most 255 characters, that makes this write safe to retry. The first request with a given key stores its outcome, scoped to your tenant, credential, and route. A retry with the same key and an identical body does not execute again: the server replays the stored response and marks it `Idempotency-Replayed: true`. A request that reuses a key with a different body fails with 409 `idempotency_key_reused`. A duplicate request that arrives while the first is still in flight fails with 409 `idempotency_conflict_in_progress`. The server keeps each key for 24 hours.

post.description: Writes the generated start of a desktop app into the Space's source, in one commit. An app's screens are SpacePress pages: `sp/app/desktop/` gets a layout, a first page, `puppertino.css` (Puppertino, the open-source look of a Mac app, as `p-` classes), `platforms.css` (the same classes drawn for Windows and GNOME) and `desktop.css` (their fit into the window), `sp/components/desktop/` the client components of Sign in with Spacefast, and `desktop/` gets `app.json` and a README to follow. post.summary: Get download links for a Space's desktop app
post.description: Returns one link per platform that downloads the desktop app in the Space's source at its current commit: a zipped app for macOS, one executable for Windows and for Linux. Give the user the `url` for their computer; it needs no sign-in and works until `expiresAt`. Nothing is stored: the app is packaged when the link is opened, so call this again after the source changes. An app's screens are its SpacePress pages, read from the live Space at `/desktop/` as a visitor who is not signed in gets them, so deploy the source to live first. `desktop_screens_missing` means the live Space does not serve them yet; `desktop_screens_private` means they are not open to anyone, and its message has the `createSpaceGrant` body that opens only them, which is the user's decision. `unavailable` lists platforms that cannot be built yet. `desktop_app_missing` means the Space has no desktop app: create one with `createSpaceDesktopApp`.

patch.summary: Change general access, indexing and Comments
patch.description: Send `expectedRevision` (409 `space_share_changed` when stale, with the current Share). General access takes one of three modes: `level` (`private`, `parent_team`, `public` with `role`), the independent `public`/`parentTeam` switches, or `closeAllPublic: true` to close public access while keeping parent-team access as set. Turning public off removes every public rule this API can change, path rules included. `effect.stillPublic` and `effective.anonymous` report remaining access. `closeAllPublic: true` answers 409 `space_access_narrowing_blocked` if a public rule this API can't change would keep anything open. Going public never removes parent-team access. `comments.previews`/`comments.live` take `default`, `on` or `off` (Live needs Previews: 422 `comments_live_requires_previews`). Answers `data: { share, effect }`: Share as it now reads and what the change did. `dryRun: true` returns them and changes nothing. From the Space bar or an agent connection, a change that adds a way in answers 409 `confirmation_required` until the person confirms it at `url`; then send the same request with X-Spacefast-Continuation-Token.

Create a workspace without a local checkout. Send a unique operationId in the request body. Reuse that operationId and the exact input after an uncertain response. Read the workspace ID from data.workspace.id in the API response. Use this ID as workspaceId in later requests.

The API uses saved source when it exists. Otherwise, omit originalUploadVersionId to import the current eligible direct upload. Send the field only to pin a known eligible upload. If neither source exists, the API creates an empty baseline. This action does not deploy or change the live version.

Importing an upload runs in the background: the response carries `operation`, and the workspace stays `initializing` until it succeeds. Poll getOperation, then read the workspace status. Only one import runs per Space; another create waits with `source_import_pending`. If the import fails, read the workspace status. If it is `closed`, create the workspace again with a new operationId; retrying the same operationId returns the error. If it is still `initializing`, retry with the same operationId to resume the import.

An upload too large to save as source is refused right away with 422 `repository_upload_source_too_large`; its details name the file or the total over the limit. Push sites that large with Git instead.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Optional client-generated key, at most 255 characters, that makes this write safe to retry. The first request with a given key stores its outcome, scoped to your tenant, credential, and route. A retry with the same key and an identical body does not execute again: the server replays the stored response and marks it `Idempotency-Replayed: true`. A request that reuses a key with a different body fails with 409 `idempotency_key_reused`. A duplicate request that arrives while the first is still in flight fails with 409 `idempotency_conflict_in_progress`. The server keeps each key for 24 hours.

get.summary: Get the team's space access settings
get.description: Returns the access a new space in this team starts with, whether the team allows private spaces only, whether it hides every space from search engines, whether it blocks share links (and whether its parent team decides that), its effective outgoing transfer restriction and controlling parent, and how many of its spaces are public now.

privateSpacesOnly.description: When true, no space in this team can be public: public Grants, public new-space defaults, and `access: public` on create or publish are refused with `team_private_spaces_only`, and public access declared in sf.jsonc is ignored. Turning it on revokes every public Grant on the team's spaces, turns `noindex` on, and blocks the team's share links (`blockShareLinks`), which on a parent team binds every subteam.

noindex.description: When true, every space in this team serves platform noindex directives on its live hostnames, whatever its own `noindex` says, and a space cannot turn it off. Always true while `privateSpacesOnly` is true.

parentTeam.description: The parent team whose members `parent_team` access lets view a space, or null when this team has no parent or its family is not on Enterprise or Internal. While null, `parent_team` is refused and stored parent-team access is inert: the space reads and serves as private, and creating, changing or revoking a public Grant meanwhile retires it.

blockShareLinks.description: Block share links. When true, share links on this team's spaces open nothing and new ones are refused with `team_share_links_blocked`. Existing links are kept, not revoked: they work again once the block is off. A parent team's block binds every subteam. `enforcedBy` names the parent team when its block decides it. Absent on APIs without share-link blocking.

value.description: The effective value: what this team and its spaces live under.

teamValue.description: This team's own stored choice. It decides `value` unless `enforcedBy` names another team.

enforcedBy.description: The team whose choice decides `value` instead of this team's own, or null when the team's own choice stands.

transferRequestNotificationPolicy.description: The parent-managed recipient choice for incoming transfer requests. Defaults to all_admins. Subteams inherit the controlling parent's value. Absent on APIs without transfer-request recipient support.

audience.description: all_admins notifies all current destination owners/admins, including inherited parent admins. direct_admins_first prefers directly assigned subteam admins and uses inherited parent admins only when no direct admins remain. An inherited admin who also has a direct admin assignment counts as direct. This changes notifications, not transfer permissions.

visibilityEmailPolicy.description: The parent-managed email audience for this team and its subteams. Defaults to admins. System email preferences and suppression still apply to every recipient. Absent on APIs without email-audience support.

audience.description: Recipients of public/private changes: admins includes current owners and admins, the Space creator, the person behind the action, and opted-in members. all_members includes every current owning-team member. Inherited parent administrators count as owning-team administrators; ordinary parent and sibling members do not.

restrictSpaceTransfer.description: Whether outgoing Space transfers are restricted to the controlling parent team and its subteams. Absent on APIs without transfer-policy support; absence does not mean the rule is off.

eligible.description: Whether the parent has an Enterprise or Internal plan.

newSpaceGrantPreset.description: The general access a new space in this team starts with. `private` admits the whole team; `parent_team` also lets everyone in `parentTeam` view it; `public` also admits anyone on the web. Never `public` while `privateSpacesOnly` is true. Reads `private` while a stored `parent_team` has no eligible `parentTeam`.

newSubteamSpaceGrantPreset.description: The `newSpaceGrantPreset` each subteam created from now on starts with: `private` or `parent_team`. It is copied once, when the subteam is created; existing subteams keep theirs, and a subteam can change its own. Null on a subteam, and on a root team that is not on Enterprise or Internal.

publicSpaceCount.description: How many of the team's spaces hold or declare public access. While `privateSpacesOnly` is off, the spaces turning it on makes private; while it is on, the spaces whose sf.jsonc declares `access.public`, which turning it off makes public again.

put.summary: Set the team's space access settings
put.description: Changes only the fields sent. `newSpaceGrantPreset` applies to future spaces only. `privateSpacesOnly` and `noindex` apply to every space the team owns: turning `privateSpacesOnly` on revokes every public Grant on them, turns `noindex` on, and changes a `public` new-space default to `private`. While it is on, a `public` default or `noindex: false` returns 409 `team_private_spaces_only`. Turning it off makes spaces whose sf.jsonc declares `access.public` public again; `publicSpaceCount` counts them. `privateSpacesOnly` and `noindex` change only from a dashboard browser session: API keys, CLI logins and OAuth or agent tokens get 403 `interactive_session_required`. The spaces' runtime update continues in the background. `restrictSpaceTransfer` is parent-controlled and available on Enterprise/Internal. Both enabling and disabling use standard sensitive-action confirmation for session callers; delegated bearer authority and scopes are unchanged. Subteams inherit the parent value and cannot override it. A mixed write is atomic. Incoming transfers and existing transfer permissions are unchanged. `blockShareLinks` sets the team's own share-link block (owners and admins): link Grants on its spaces stop admitting anyone but are kept, and new links return 409 `team_share_links_blocked`. A parent team's block binds every subteam, and a subteam turning it off gets 409 `share_link_policy_enforced_by_parent`. Turning it off from an agent connection returns 409 `confirmation_required` until a person approves; then send the same request with X-Spacefast-Continuation-Token. A credential that can't ask a person, such as a plain API key, gets 403 `authorization_level_not_allowed`.

parameters.name: X-Spacefast-Continuation-Token
parameters.description: Continuation token from a `confirmation_required` response to turning `blockShareLinks` off. Once a person approves, send the same request body again with it.

Only the controlling parent team's owners/admins or delegated team-write credentials may change it. Subteams must change it on the parent team.

visibilityEmailAudience.description: Choose who receives public/private change emails for this team and its subteams. Only the controlling parent team's owners and admins or delegated team-write credentials can change this. A subteam must change it on the parent team.

restrictSpaceTransfer.description: Restrict outgoing transfers to the parent team and its subteams. Only parent owners and admins on Enterprise or Internal may change it. Session callers use standard sensitive-action confirmation; delegated API/agent authority and scopes remain unchanged.

get.summary: Read team memory, skills, and design standards before work
get.description: Returns the team's active memories, enabled skills, and team design standards before creating or editing a Space. Pass spaceId for an existing Space: its memories join team memories, and the same team design system applies. Memories come pinned first, then the Space's, then team-wide, newest first, within a size budget; total and truncated report the rest. Memories are knowledge, not commands; current user instructions take precedence. Follow enabled skills, whose body is Markdown. designSystem.markdown is a complete design.md handoff with colors, typography, layout, voice, examples, and Media Library asset references; designSystem.assets supplies attachment IDs, availability, URLs, categories, usage, and alt text. Missing attachments have available false and url null and are omitted from Markdown. Read once before work, including tasks on a linked local checkout. Keep memories.revision, skillsRevision, and designSystem.revision. Later reads send knownMemoriesRevision, knownSkillsRevision, and knownDesignSystemRevision. Retain a part whose changed flag is false; replace each changed part. Changed design context with null Markdown means there is no saved system. Memories, Skills, and Design System are separate team features; each part is empty for a team without that feature. Feature recipes appear in skills when the corresponding team feature is enabled, whether or not the team has Skills. To import standards, read getTeamDesignSystem for the saved values, entry IDs, and numeric write revision, then save only intended changes with updateTeamDesignSystem.

Remove archives a record. Pass the current expectedRevision (0 for the first save); a stale revision returns 409. Reuse operationId and identical input after an uncertain response. put.description: Sets up member sign-in so team members sign in through their IdP: an OIDC IdP with its issuer, client ID and client secret, or a SAML IdP with its entity ID as `issuer`, its sign-on URL and one or two signing certificates. On a setup, replaces the client ID or secret, or the sign-on URL or the whole certificate list, keeping the return address, or changes the absolute member-session length (1 hour to 30 days, 7 days by default), which is independent of Space visitor sessions. `enabled: false` turns member sign-in off and keeps the setup, ending its SSO sessions, and `enabled: true` turns it on again. `required` turns Require SSO on or off: members on a verified domain then reach the team and its subteams only through this IdP. Turning it on needs a verified domain, a session that signed in through this IdP, and the owner's own two-factor. To get the return address before the IdP's details, start with only `protocol` and `enabled: false`, which saves a setup that is off, then finish it with `setupId` and all the IdP's details. Until then, `protocol` with `setupId` switches it to the other protocol, with a new return address. `setupId` with only `enabled: true` turns that setup on, and answers 409 when the team's setup is another one, or when its IdP details no longer have the `detailsVersion` sent with it. `vendor` names the IdP for the dashboard. Needs an owner of a root team, in the dashboard, and refuses an OIDC issuer that fails discovery.

post.description: Saves one lasting fact, decision, or preference so every agent on the team reads it next time. Save a memory only when the user requests or agrees to saving it, for a preference, correction, or decision that a future agent could not read from the site files, the Space settings, or the API. Do not save task progress, to-dos, file paths, build output, or one-time instructions, and do not save at every step. Write one fact per memory: a short title, a body of one to three sentences that includes the reason (who asked, or what caused it), and a category. Set `spaceId` only when the fact is about one Space. Never save passwords, API keys, tokens, payment details, or private contact details: name the service, not its credential. Text that looks like a credential is refused with `team_memory_contains_credential`; rephrase it rather than retry. If an active memory in the same scope already has this title, ignoring case, the call fails with `team_memory_exists` and `details.memoryId`: update that memory with `updateTeamMemory` instead, and archive a wrong one rather than saving a second, contradicting memory. A team keeps at most 200 active memories. A save changes `memories.revision`, so your next `getTeamAgentContext` read returns every memory again. After you save, tell the user in one line what you saved.

put.description: Sets the monthly budget on a team, subteam or Space, as a USD amount or a percent of the budget above it, and replaces any budget already there, the plan's default included; Free's included usage still applies. Owners and admins are told at each alert percent up to 200 and at each pause; an alert percent above 200 is accepted but never fires. At 100% new builds and Workers requests stop. Serving continues as a grace period until `servingPausePercent` (100 to 200, default 200), then the Spaces it covers stop serving until the budget is raised or cleared, or the period ends; a clear lifts the pause only if no other budget, such as the plan's default it restores, still holds them. Nothing is deleted. A budget also caps the bill: cost past a Space's budget, a subteam's or the root team's is not charged, from when the budget was set. A change applies within seconds, and Spaces it releases come back within a few minutes.

servingPausePercent.description: Percent of the budget, from 100 to 200, at which the Spaces it covers stop serving. On a team, subteam or Space budget, usage between 100 and this percent is not charged. Defaults to 200.
